run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T23:29:38Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for frontend-proxy/otel-demo is backed by real, but small and bursty, error traffic on the proxy's own ingress spans. Sampled error ratio for frontend-proxy ingress spans was 1.148% (23:00-23:15), 0.085% (23:15-23:30) and 1.18% (23:30-23:45), so this was never a sustained high error rate. The error counter shows two populations: (1) a slow-request burst at 23:09:51-23:10:26 where the proxy logged 504 UT response_timeout on /api/data (15s upstream timeout) while the frontend's own >5s spans were internal "GET" spans and every dependency client span had 0 >5s spans; (2) a jump of ~93 ingress error spans between 23:32 and 23:34, matching 500 via_upstream responses on /api/cart and /api/checkout logged 23:32:36-23:32:52, coinciding with the cart Deployment being rollout-restarted at 23:32:08 (annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt, generation 2, same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart) and with frontend tcp.connect failures. A background of ~1 503 upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} per 1-2 minutes runs through the whole window. The cart service emitted no error spans in the sampled windows, so the frontend's cart calls failed at connection level during the pod replacement rather than with observed cart application errors. The only switched-on fault-injection setting found is cartFailure="on" ("Fail cart service") in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config; it is named as the root cause object per the fault-injection rule, but the declared cart fault was not observed firing and its change time could not be determined, so the conclusion is partial. A separate fraud-detection container OOMKill at 23:37:38 is not tied to these errors.

claims.text: frontend-proxy ingress spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR: increase over 23:30-23:50 is ~107.6 error spans against ~9001 STATUS_CODE_UNSET ingress spans (and ~97.2 vs ~9010.8 on its "router frontend egress" client span), so the service's own error signal is nonzero but roughly 1% of span volume.

The frontend-proxy ingress error ratio computed from traces_span_metrics_calls_total was 0.0114899 (23:00-23:15), 0.0008499 (23:15-23:30) and 0.0118173 (23:30-23:45); the first and third 15-minute buckets are where the error ratio reached the ~1.1% scale reported in the alert annotation.

The raw frontend-proxy ingress error counter went 594 (23:25) -> 596 (23:32) -> 689 (23:34) -> 692 (23:35) -> 698 (23:48): a one-off jump of ~93 between 23:32 and 23:34 plus ~1 error per 1-2 minutes otherwise.

frontend-proxy access logs show "500 - via_upstream" responses for GET/POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout from 23:32:36 to 23:32:52, followed by 200 responses from 23:33:03 onward, matching the counter jump in the 23:32-23:34 interval.

The frontend service's own error spans in 23:30-23:50 are concentrated on cart/checkout operations: grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 54.4, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 24.1, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 18.8, GET /api/cart 24.1, POST /api/cart 54.4, POST /api/checkout 18.8 and tcp.connect 7.3 error spans, while its GetAds call and /api/data route show 0.

In 5-minute resolution the frontend's cart-related error spans appear in exactly one bucket (evaluated 23:35, i.e. roughly 23:30-23:35): GET /api/cart 25.6, POST /api/cart 57.8, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 57.8, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 25.6; the 23:40 and 23:45 buckets are 0.
The frontend's tcp.connect span counter rose from 37 (steady 23:25-23:32) to 45 at 23:35 and stayed 45, i.e. +8 connection attempts failed in the same interval as the cart 500 burst.

Kubernetes events in otel-demo at 23:32:08-23:32:11 record a cart controller rollout: Deployment cart ScalingReplicaSet 0->1 on cart-84889c965d, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz, Pod Killing cart-755465879b-rh5r4, ReplicaSet cart-755465879b SuccessfulDelete, Deployment cart ScalingReplicaSet 1->0.

The cart Deployment's pod template carries annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt = 2026-11-17T23:32:08Z, its generation is 2 and its container image is still ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart, i.e. it was restarted with an unchanged pod template; ReplicaSet cart-755465879b was created 23:00:58 and cart-84889c965d 23:32:08.

The replacement cart pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz started 23:32:08, its init container wait-for-valkey-cart completed 23:32:09, the cart container started 23:32:10 and the pod reported Ready/ContainersReady at 23:32:11 with restartCount 0; the cart container defines neither a readinessProbe nor a livenessProbe.

ConfigMap flagd-config (otel-demo) contains flag cartFailure with defaultVariant "on", description "Fail cart service" and state ENABLED, a fault-injection setting that is switched on and names the cart service.

Every other fault-injection flag in the same flagd-config data (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) has defaultVariant "off".

The cart service's own spans in 23:20-23:45 carry no STATUS_CODE_ERROR at all (GetCart/AddItem/EmptyCart and the Valkey HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE spans are STATUS_CODE_UNSET), with GetCart ~735-920 per 5 min and AddItem ~406-478 per 5 min; the only dip is GetCart 735 in the 23:30-23:35 bucket versus 845-920 in the neighbouring buckets.

The cart container's logs for 23:32-23:42 contain 3382 lines, all normal "GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync/EmptyCartAsync called" entries with no failure text among the lines shown; its previous container instance does not exist, so nothing older is available.

Before the alert the proxy's errors were slow-request timeouts: frontend-proxy logged "504 UT response_timeout" for GET /api/data?contextKeys=... requests between 23:09:51 and 23:10:26 with 15s upstream response times, and 32 ingress spans exceeded 10s in the 23:10-23:15 bucket (0 in every later bucket).

In the 23:10-23:15 bucket the frontend's only spans slower than 5s were 45.1 internal spans with span_name "GET"; its dependency client spans (grpc.oteldemo.CartService/*, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, RecommendationService/ListRecommendations, AdService/GetAds) were all 0 >5s, and no dependency service other than accounting (constant 5-13 >5s spans per bucket, background) had >5s spans.

A background of 503 upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} responses is present throughout: frontend-proxy logged them on /api/products, /api/data, /api/recommendations and /api/cart at 23:10:40, 23:11:36, 23:13:08, 23:15:12, 23:20:33, 23:28:25 and 23:30:25, roughly one per 1-2 minutes, before and after the alert start.

In 23:00-23:20 the proxy's ingress spans already carried 36.6 error spans, yet every frontend span in that window had 0 errors (GET, GET/POST /api/*, grpc.oteldemo.* client spans and tcp.connect), so the 504 timeouts have no matching frontend error span.
The fraud-detection container in pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh was OOMKilled at 23:37:38 (exitCode 137, reason OOMKilled) and restarted, reaching Ready again at 23:37:40 with restartCount 1.

The switched-on cartFailure flag in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config is the configured fault behind the cart failures that surfaced as frontend 500s on /api/cart and /api/checkout; because the cart service's own sampled spans show no failure, the flag's effect was not directly observed, so this remains a hypothesis rather than a proven mechanism.

The 23:32 burst was produced by the cart Deployment rollout restart at 23:32:08: because the cart container has no readiness probe, the replacement pod was declared Ready at 23:32:11 while its gRPC server was apparently not yet accepting connections, so frontend cart/checkout calls failed at connection level until 23:32:52. This explains the largest error burst but not the alert's start 2.5 minutes earlier.

The pre-alert portion of the error rate (15s 504 timeouts on /api/data at 23:09:51-23:10:26 and the recurring 503 connection_termination responses) originates in the frontend/Envoy-to-frontend path rather than in a downstream service, because no dependency had slow or failing spans; what blocked the frontend is not determinable from the available evidence (no frontend logs, no frontend traces).

The declared cart fault was not observed firing: the cart service emitted hundreds of AddItem/GetCart spans per 5 minutes with no error status, so the frontend's cart/checkout errors are consistent with connection-level failures during the pod replacement rather than with cart returning application errors.
The cart rollout restart cannot explain the alert's start: the alert fired at 23:29:38, while the restart annotation and controller events are at 23:32:08 and the 500 responses begin at 23:32:36.

The fraud-detection container OOMKill is not the source of the checkout errors: the OOMKill occurred at 23:37:38, after the frontend's PlaceOrder error spans in the 23:30-23:35 bucket, and fraud-detection reported no error spans in 23:30-23:50, so it is a separate restart reason (container memory limit exceeded) unrelated to this alert.
Switch cartFailure back to off in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config and confirm the effective value flagd serves to the cart service, so the declared 'Fail cart service' fault is not left armed.

Add a readiness (or startup) probe to the cart container so the pod is not added to the Service endpoint before its gRPC listener accepts connections, and avoid single-replica cart rollout restarts during load; that would have prevented the 23:32:36-23:32:52 500 burst.

To explain the frontend-side latency and the recurring connection_termination 503s, capture frontend container output (it produced no log lines here) and keep frontend traces, and review the frontend-proxy to frontend keep-alive/idle timeout settings.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alert rule is not present in the queried Prometheus: the rule query for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and the type=alert listing both returned no data, so the alert's expression, evaluation window and the request population behind the reported value 0.01111111111111111 (exactly 1/90) are unknown.

Cannot determine when cartFailure was switched to "on": there is no change-history integration available and ConfigMaps expose no modification timestamp; the flag is on now while the cart errors have stopped.

The declared cart fault itself was not observed: no cart-side error spans were found, and an error-word-filtered log query on the cart container returned no matching lines (an empty result only shows that query matched nothing), so it cannot be confirmed that the cartFailure flag produced the failed frontend cart/checkout calls.
Unknown what applied the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation to Deployment cart at 2026-11-17T23:32:08Z (no actor or change record is available); the restart happened after the alert start.

The frontend container produced no log lines at all in 23:30-23:50 and its error-filtered query in 23:25-23:50 returned no matching lines, and Jaeger returned no frontend or frontend-proxy traces for 23:30-23:50, so the cause of the >15s frontend responses at 23:09:51-23:10:26 and of the periodic connection_termination resets is unknown.

kube-state-metrics series are absent from this Prometheus (kube_pod_container_info, kube_pod_owner, kube_replicaset_owner, kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready and the kube_.* metric-name listing all returned no data), so pod readiness/replica history and an old-vs-new cart image digest comparison could not be obtained; the unchanged-image conclusion rests on the identical image tag ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart.
Span metrics only begin around 23:00 in this environment, so there is no comparable baseline from before 23:00 and I cannot say whether the observed ~1% error ratio is abnormal for this deployment.

frontend-proxy log reads hit the 4 MiB read limit for 23:00-23:32 and were incomplete for 23:25-23:50, so some access-log lines in those intervals were not read; the 504/503 evidence cited covers only the lines actually read.
The flagd pod's log query for 23:00-23:50 returned no matching lines, so flagd's own view of flag state changes could not be checked.
Impact beyond frontend-proxy, frontend and the cart/checkout call path (e.g. end-user or load-generator-visible failure rate) was not measured and remains unverified.
